name: calibrated_v3
summary: Optional changes beyond Shiu et al. 2024 that keep antennal-lobe output glomerulus-specific, Kenyon cell odour codes sparse and distinct, and stop latching, without changing the published sugar->MN9, bitter->MN9 and looming->Giant Fibre results.

adaptation.rationale: spike-frequency adaptation; removes self-sustained (latched) activity. Antennal-lobe local neurons get 1 mV more per spike (1.2 mV total) so the LN network cannot keep itself active after an odour

slow_inhibition.scope: antennal-lobe local neurons (class ALLN) with inhibitory sign
slow_inhibition.rationale: not needed once eLN->PN transmission is corrected; at 0.5 (v1) it held uniglomerular PNs at ~6 Hz instead of ~100 Hz

al_excitatory_ln.scope: connections from antennal-lobe local neurons with excitatory sign (FlyWire: mostly lLN1/lLN2 types; Janelia MaleCNS: cholinergic)
al_excitatory_ln.rationale: excitatory LNs reach projection neurons mainly through gap junctions; blocking chemical transmission leaves eLN->PN excitation intact (Yaksi & Wilson 2010, Neuron 67:1034; Huang et al. 2010, Neuron 67:1021 find cholinergic + electrical). The connectome records only chemical synapses, which the model turns into full-strength fast excitation: one receptor type then drives ~70% of all PNs. Chemical eLN->PN and eLN->eLN transmission is scaled to 10%; eLN->inhibitory LN is kept

calibration: cognition/calibrate_dynamics.py grids eln, eln_mix, eln2 + held-out mixture sets (Mac, 2026-09-25)
held_out: 4 mixture sets x 10 odours (6 random olfactory glomeruli, 30-80 Hz), simulation seeds 1/3/5/11
known_limits: after some mixtures a few thousand spikes persist for >200 ms in the central complex / LAL (PFR, LAL112, CRE008: the heading-circuit attractor) and optic-lobe Lawf2; the published model latches ~100k
gap-junction lateral excitation between glomeruli is not modelled (the engine has chemical synapses only)

orn_pn_compensation.scope: olfactory receptor neuron -> antennal-lobe projection neuron connections
orn_pn_compensation.rule: per projection neuron, multiply its ORN connections by (mean synapses per ORN connection of its cell type, both sides) / (its own mean synapses per ORN connection)
orn_pn_compensation.rationale: Tobin, Wilson & Lee 2017 (eLife 6:e24838): PNs with more ORN synapses have larger dendrites and lower input resistance, so unitary connection strength is the same on the left and right despite different synapse numbers. The model's uniform per-synapse weight drops this compensation; in FlyWire the left PNs of some glomeruli receive 25-50% more ORN synapses than the right (DM1, VM3, VA2, VM2), which made odour responses left-dominant. Relative ipsi/contra strength within each PN is kept (odour lateralization).

giant_fibre.rationale: The Giant Fibre's low input resistance and ~1.6 ms time constant make each synapse worth ~0.3x that of a typical descending neuron (fitted per-synapse depolarisation at the spike initiation zone 0.045-0.061 vs 0.16-0.19 mV for DNp03; Moreno-Sanchez et al. 2024; Ceballos et al. 2026 use 25 vs 300 MOhm). Johnston's organ -> GF transmission is electrical (unaffected by Cd2+, abolished in shakB mutants; Lehnert et al. 2013; Pezier et al. 2016) and sub-threshold on its own (Blagburn 2020); the model has no gap junctions, so these chemical edges are removed. Real GF: no spikes at rest or to air puffs / sound alone (Mu et al. 2014).
giant_fibre.calibration: 0.3 left the GF at 0.75 Hz under resting ORN input; 0.2 (inside the 0.083-0.35 bracket) gives 0 Hz at rest while looming still drives it to 210 Hz (was 353). 2026-09-25, cognition/calibrate_dynamics.py gf_rest_hz/gf_loom.
giant_fibre.threshold_rationale: The model's threshold is 7 mV above rest (-52 -> -45 mV, Shiu et al. 2024); the Giant Fibre's is ~10 mV above rest (Blagburn 2020, PLoS One 15:e0224057). The membrane is linear below threshold, so a 10 mV gap is equivalent to scaling its inputs by 7/10 (applied on top of chemical_input_scale).

heading_input.route: Poisson drive to E-PG neurons at the current heading (landmark-like, as visual ring neurons provide); brain/navigation/compass.CompassDrive
heading_input.heading_source: the body's integrated angular velocity (robot IMU/odometry or the simulated body): path integration outside the connectome

central_complex.calibration: Mac, 2026-09-25, whole brain with calibrated dynamics + resting ORN input. Unmodified ring (gain 1.0): heading at 0/90/180/270 deg read back within 1-10 deg; heading rotating at 45/90/180/-90 deg/s tracked with median error 4-6 deg. Bump does not persist without input (< 250 ms).

alternatives_tested.persistence: removing adaptation from ring neurons and scaling ring-internal synapses x1.3-1.5 makes a seeded bump persist (x1.5: >= 3 s from every seed, strength ~0.8; x2.0 runs away), but the bump is pinned to one or two preferred positions (with resting input all seeds end at the same phase); per-neuron input normalisation within the ring and 4-8 Hz tonic ring input (Kakaria & de Bivort 2017 used 5 Hz) did not remove the pinning. With these settings landmark tracking degrades (x1.4: dropouts drift up to 170 deg).
alternatives_tested.angular_velocity: graded (add_g 1-20) or Poisson bias to P-EN1 (and P-EN1+P-EN2) on one side did not rotate the bump in opposite directions for left vs right (< 25 deg/s, inconsistent signs). P-EN1 is silenced by strong inhibition from ExR6 (~220-310 Hz, 4,456 synapses) and GLNO (65-180 Hz, 4,834 synapses; sign inferred, NT unknown).

central_complex.rationale: Seelig & Jayaraman 2015 Nature 521:186 (E-PG heading bump); Green et al. 2017 Nature 546:101 and Turner-Evans et al. 2017 eLife 6:e23496 (P-EN velocity integration); Kakaria & de Bivort 2017 Front Behav Neurosci 11:8 (spiking PB/EB ring attractor moved by sensory-like E-PG input, same LIF parameters as Shiu et al. 2024).

goal_input.route: Poisson drive to FC2 neurons tuned to the goal direction (Gaussian over each cell's goal column); brain/navigation/goal.GoalDrive
goal_input.columns: PFL3/PFL2 PB angle from their E-PG inputs (compass.glom_angle, mirrored between PB halves; confirmed by E-PG -> Delta7 pairing L_g <-> R_(10-g)); FC2 goal column = synapse-weighted circular mean of the PB angles of the PFL3 cells it contacts
goal_input.calibration: Mac, 2026-09-25: PFL3 R-L and DNa02 R-L change sign with goal - heading (zero within ~15 deg) at headings 0/90/270 deg; PFL2 lowest at goal = heading; closed loop go-home 3/6 vs 1/6 (goal off) with the default body, 5/6 vs 1/6 with 30 deg/s turning noise
goal_input.rationale: Westeinde et al. 2024 Nature 626:819; Mussells Pires et al. 2024 Nature 626:808 (FC2 goal, PFL3 comparison -> DNa02 steering; PFL2 far-from-goal)

orn_short_term_depression.scope: every output synapse of olfactory receptor neurons (ORN_* types)
orn_short_term_depression.rule: presynaptic depletion d per ORN: a spike transmits (1 - d) of full strength and leaves d = 1 - (1 - d) * 0.78; d recovers to 0 with tau 893 ms (native engines: lif_set_std)
orn_short_term_depression.rationale: ORN->PN synapses depress (Kazama & Wilson 2008, Neuron 58:401), and presynaptic inhibition limits that depression (Nagel, Hong & Wilson 2015, Nat Neurosci 18:56). The depression per spike is FITTED to the measured ORN->PN transform (Olsen, Bhandawat & Wilson 2010, Neuron 66:287: PN = Rmax ORN^1.5/(ORN^1.5 + sigma^1.5), Rmax 144-170 Hz, sigma 12-45 Hz) for glomeruli DL5 and DM1 and the resting uPN rate; DA1 held out. Grid f 0.90/0.95/0.97 x full-strength gain 1/1.5/2: f 0.95 and 0.97 at gain 1 fit best (13/15 points in the measured band); 0.97 was chosen because 0.95 latched after odours (0.16) and steered asymmetrically. tau 893 ms from the agent-summarised Nagel et al. model (value not verified against the paper).

orn_pn_lateral_release.scope: ORN -> uniglomerular/multiglomerular PN connections (class ALPN), split by ORN side vs PN soma side
orn_pn_lateral_release.rationale: Each ORN axon projects to both antennal lobes; the ipsilateral branch releases ~40% more transmitter per spike, so ipsilateral PNs respond more and flies can steer toward the side with more odour (Gaudry, Hong, Kain, de Bivort & Wilson 2013, Nature 493:424). Release probability is invisible in EM, so the connectome's synapse counts miss it. Ipsi x 2r/(1+r), contra x 2/(1+r), r = 1.4.

bilateral_consensus.rule: for every (presynaptic type, side) -> (postsynaptic type, side) connection group, the mean synapse count per postsynaptic cell is set to the mean of the group and its left-right mirror (multiplier clipped to 0.5-2); unpaired types unchanged
bilateral_consensus.rationale: FAFB is one individual; its left-right differences mix individual variation with reconstruction differences (Schlegel et al. 2024, Nature 634:139: e.g. the left DM3 adPN, right ALl1-ventral dendrites, 6% calyx completion). Individual flies have lasting turning biases but the population is unbiased (Buchanan, Kain & de Bivort 2015, PNAS 112:6700). Without this the resting brain turns left: DNa02 14 vs 4 Hz, driven by e.g. LAL051->DNa02 64 (left) vs 127 (right) synapses. A symmetric 'consensus' brain represents the species; individual handedness can be added back as an explicit parameter.
